correctness.rationale: For f(u)=u1u2u3, the spherical Hessian identity reduces the curvature-radius perturbation on u-perp to A=(D^2F)|_{u-perp}-2fI. The stated tangent trace -10s and determinant 16s^2+4q-1 give eigenvalues -5s plus or minus sqrt(1-4q+9s^2). After X=x^2,Y=y^2,Z=z^2, maximizing the spectral radius reduces at an interior critical point to two equal coordinates; setting Y=Z=t yields the two explicit branches in the package. Their maxima are 4sqrt(6)/9 at t=1/6 and 1 at t=3/8, so the global operator-norm maximum is 4sqrt(6)/9. An independent dense simplex replay numerically localized the maximum at a permutation of approximately (2/3,1/6,1/6) and matched 4sqrt(6)/9. Thus alpha I+beta A is positive semidefinite for every normal exactly at alpha >= (4sqrt(6)/9)|beta|, equivalently |epsilon|<=3sqrt(6)/8 when alpha=1; the sign condition leaves exactly twelve endpoint-degeneracy normals.

Its proof uses continuity of the curvature-radius operator and does not state a sharp admissible interval or endpoint degeneracy set. Resultary search found the assigned exact threshold as the direct match; a related published SCOPE result gives a general degree-three harmonic curvature bound and a different Wigner-cubic constant, not this xyz-family optimum.
